The newly unveiled **EP-35** is engineered to handle multiple sound sources simultaneously, accommodating various instruments through its multi-input architecture. According to **The Verge**, the battery-operated speaker system is built for mobility, offering players a self-contained setup for on-the-go practice or street performances. 

While portable instrument amplifiers have traditionally focused on straightforward amplification, this model integrates comprehensive signal processing capabilities natively into the chassis. Reviewers note that the manufacturer's approach mirrors its previous pocket-sized synthesizers and studio gear, which prioritize tactile interfaces and compact footprints. For readers tracking broader shifts in the technology hardware sector, hardware manufacturers are increasingly rethinking traditional form factors—much like how software developers recently shifted strategies, as seen in how the [Arc browser sunsets December 22 as The Browser Company doubles down on Dia](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/arc-browser-sunsets-december-as-the-browser-company-doubles-down-on-dia).

The controversial campaign spot prominently features Acton's estranged mother, whose husband faced charges of sexual abuse during Acton's childhood. In response to the broadcast, Acton did not mince words, describing the spot as "despicable" and criticizing the decision to drag deeply painful family history into the political arena. 

The inclusion of these sensitive and traumatic personal matters has sent shockwaves through the race, sparking intense debate over the boundaries of acceptable campaign strategies. While campaigns frequently clash over policy records and voting histories, leveraging estranged family members and childhood trauma marks a deeply personal escalation. The strategy has already created internal friction within the political sphere, mirroring recent tensions seen when figures like [Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' about controversial Ohio attack ad](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/vance-tells-republicans-to-stop-whining-about-controversial-ohio-attack-ad), according to related reporting.

By bringing up the actions of Acton's mother and her husband, the campaign has drawn sharp criticism from observers who argue the spot crosses ethical lines. The broadcast relies on painful historical events from Acton's youth, transforming private family trauma into public electoral ammunition. 

Political analysts point out that personal attacks of this nature are designed to shock voters and alter the momentum of a tight race. However, such aggressive tactics often risk alienating moderate voters who may view the strategy as overly mean-spirited. The stakes in this race extend far beyond the immediate candidates, shaping voter turnout and defining the tone of political engagement in the region. Two years ago, university student **Vasant Bhatt** was knocking doors for **Sen. Ted Cruz** and organizing his community for **Donald Trump** in hopes of helping Republicans regain power, but a rise in anti-Indian rhetoric within the party has since driven him and other voters away, according to a report by **The Verge**. 

## The Shift in Allegiance

The report states that what began as policy disagreements has transformed into explicit identity-based attacks from the political right. According to The Verge, young Indian Americans who previously aligned with conservative platforms report feeling alienated by xenophobic tropes circulating among high-profile figures and online commentators. The publication highlights that figures like **Vivek Ramaswamy** have faced racially charged scrutiny during campaign cycles, illustrating a broader pattern where South Asian candidates and citizens are subjected to coded or overt bigotry from within conservative circles.

Historically, immigrant communities have found common ground with conservative values centered on economic mobility, entrepreneurship, and traditional family structures. However, the report indicates that the mainstreaming of nationalist rhetoric is fraying these political alliances. Voters who once invested time and energy into conservative campaigns now describe feeling unwelcome in a movement that increasingly leans into ethnic exclusion.

## Why This Matters

As political parties aggressively court every demographic slice in competitive regions, the alienation of a fast-growing, economically influential electorate carries significant electoral consequences. For decades, minority outreach has been a central calculation in American politics; when a major party permits or ignores identity-based vitriol, it risks forfeiting a generation of upwardly mobile voters. This dynamic places heightened pressure on local organizers who must reconcile national party messaging with grassroots retention efforts, a friction that could alter turnout in critical suburban districts.

This shift mirrors broader anxieties around media representation and public accountability, echoing discussions seen in our coverage of how [Betty Gilpin seeks out 'anti-algorithm' projects, like 'The Lowdown' and 'Widow's Bay'](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/betty-gilpin-seeks-out-anti-algorithm-projects-like-the-lowdown-and-widow) to escape homogenized cultural messaging. Similarly, public figures and creators face mounting scrutiny over offensive rhetoric, much like a [Republican leader embarrassed by Ali G film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/republican-leader-embarrassed-by-ali-g-film-says-he-plans-to-sue) following humiliating public exposures.

## What to Watch

Observers will be tracking whether conservative leadership takes concrete steps to distance the party from online xenophobia or if alienating rhetoric continues unchecked through upcoming election cycles. Analysts will also monitor voter registration trends in suburban counties across Texas to measure whether disaffected volunteers permanently migrate to the political center or opposition.

In an announcement shared to the Android community help forums , Google suggests a simple fix for Canadians experiencing issues as a result … Read the full story at The Verge.
articles.aiArticle:
Google has issued an urgent advisory urging Android device owners to apply a software update immediately, following legislative shifts in Canada that have altered how certain regions handle seasonal clock changes. According to a report by **The Verge**, the warning arrives as several Canadian jurisdictions move to adopt permanent daylight saving time, exposing a vulnerability in how older mobile operating systems calculate local hours. While policymakers push for year-round evening sunlight, the underlying technical infrastructure of everyday pocket devices is struggling to keep pace with these legislative updates.

## Technical Glitches Threaten Smartphone Clocks

The root of the issue lies in outdated time zone databases embedded within mobile software, which dictate when clocks should spring forward or fall back. Without the newly released patches, affected smartphones risk displaying incorrect times, throwing off morning alarms, calendar appointments, and automated system backups. **The Verge** notes that while major technology companies frequently issue routine patches for timezone adjustments, abrupt or fragmented regional policy changes create severe logistical hurdles for automated system updates. 

This technical hiccup in North America echoes broader challenges in software stability, reminiscent of how developers routinely scramble to patch vulnerabilities across complex codebases, similar to the widespread anxiety caused when critical platforms face sudden security crises like the recent [PHP armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/php-armageddon-openai-google-s-wiz-find-ancient-holes-panicking-the-internet). Mobile operating systems rely heavily on absolute precision, meaning even minor legislative alterations to regional timekeeping can trigger cascading software failures if device internal clocks drift out of sync with official atomic time servers.

## Why This Matters

As governments increasingly tinker with historical timekeeping frameworks, the stakes for everyday consumers and global enterprise systems grow exponentially. When regional legislation clashes with fixed software logic, millions of users face immediate disruptions in their daily routines, ranging from missed flights to failed digital authentications that rely on precise time stamps. 

Historically, daylight saving time was enacted during World War I to conserve energy by extending evening daylight, yet modern society's absolute dependence on synchronized digital infrastructure means that altering these rhythms now creates disproportionate friction. For everyday citizens, a simple hour discrepancy can derail work schedules and transportation logistics, while businesses face potential synchronization errors in database logs and financial transactions.

## What to Watch

Industry observers should monitor whether other federal and state legislatures follow Canada’s lead in permanently altering seasonal time laws, which would force smartphone manufacturers to continually overhaul their default time zone libraries. Analysts will also track how effectively major tech firms push over-the-air patches to legacy hardware that no longer receives active OS support, as unpatched devices remain uniquely vulnerable to perpetual time drift.

Sources: [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1016977/google-android-incorrect-time-daylight-saving-permanent-canada)

articles.title: The Guardian view on England's north-south divide: Burnham must deliver more than devolution | Editorial
articles.summary: The prime minister promises to repair decades of regional damage. His government must redistribute wealth to close deadly inequalities Andy Burnham’s call to abandon “ 40 years of neoliberalism ” rests partly on the damage that he says it has done to northern…
articles.content: The prime minister promises to repair decades of regional damage. His government must redistribute wealth to close deadly inequalities Andy Burnham’s call to abandon “ 40 years of neoliberalism ” rests partly on the damage that he says it has done to northern England. A new study – published in the Lancet this week – adds weight to his argument. It found that for adults aged 25 to 49, death rates in the north were 13% higher than in the south in 1981. By 2024, that gap had more than tripled to 42%. What happened in the four decades that left younger adults in northern England with so much worse chances of survival? The answer lies in the lives and jobs that people have, and the homes they can afford, as well as the state of the public services, like the NHS, that they rely on. Deindustrialisation stripped secure employment from many communities in the north of England – as it did in Scotland and Wales. Austerity then weakened support systems. These reasons also underscore Mr Burnham’s analysis that Britain’s economic model and concentration of power in London have failed its regions. Continue reading...

articles.aiArticle:
Websites globally are facing a massive wave of security threats as malicious actors launch millions of automated attempts to exploit a severe vulnerability in the PHP programming language, according to **Business | The Guardian**. The high-volume attacks have forced both corporate networks and government entities to take drastic action, including pulling web portals offline entirely to install urgent security patches.

PHP serves as the digital foundation for a vast majority of the internet, powering approximately **70%** of all sites online. Because of this widespread ubiquity, the sudden discovery of a critical code flaw has triggered an unprecedented scramble among system administrators. As digital defenses race against automated exploit tools, understanding the technical nature of this emergency is vital, leading many to examine [what PHP is and how bad the computer language flaw is](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/what-is-php-and-how-bad-is-the-computer-language-flaw-causing) as organizations struggle to contain the fallout.

## Global Fallout and Mitigation Efforts

According to the report, the scale of the incident has caught many digital infrastructure teams off guard. articles.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
articles.summary: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner.…
articles.content: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa president Gianni Infantino dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. articles.summary: Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger . By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and…
articles.content: Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger . By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and platforms, including DeviantArt and 4Chan, which were temporarily shut down after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Even governments weren’t immune. But it’s not as simple as updating a few servers. The vulnerability exists in every version of PHP dating back roughly 20 years, many of which are no longer supported. That means some older sites and services that are no longer actively maintained are at risk, leaving them with little option but to permanently shut down. Here’s all the latest developments in what security firm Wiz has called “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered … in software history.” The Internet Archive was briefly forced offline because of PHP. Two old-school Japanese mobile games are shutting down over the PHP exploit. The PHP2Shell exploit hit Cloudflare hard. PHP: The three letters that shut down sites all over the internet today GPT‑5.6 Sol was used to identify critical PHP flaw. A critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today

articles.title: Ali G: Who Iz I? review – Sacha Baron Cohen’s high-stakes satire punches up and down with spectacular bad taste
articles.summary: Baron Cohen’s live-ammo prankster is back, 20 years on, but has to battle with his own irrelevance in search of big laughs and the approval of a new generation • Exclusive: Republican leader embarrassed by film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar…
articles.content: Baron Cohen’s live-ammo prankster is back, 20 years on, but has to battle with his own irrelevance in search of big laughs and the approval of a new generation • Exclusive: Republican leader embarrassed by film says he plans to sue Sacha Baron Cohen: ‘A liar and a pervert’ If you liked Sacha Baron Cohen’s Ali G the first time around, you’ll like this less; if you disliked it, you’ll dislike this more; if you suspected it was racist, you’ll be more emboldened to say so – especially as Baron Cohen has dreamed up a whole new character apparently to pre-empt and mock precisely that objection. Broad and crass as it often is – in fact always is – this Ali G sequel is sometimes funny: the athletic vigour of our hero’s pranking and punking is like the umpteenth Jackass film at which you might find yourself laughing, and Baron Cohen blunders with the semi-intentional force of an XL bully into the issue of whether jokes are still allowed. Unlike the first film, Ali G in Da House from 2002, this is not a full written-through narrative. It is basically another live-ammo series of hoaxes with some spectacular bad taste perpetrated upon the deserving and less deserving; it satirises the shamelessness of anti-woke free speech martyrs, punching up and down with grossout cringe, and the targets include some big names who shouldn’t be revealed here. There are two other subordinate characters: Erran Morad, a sinister Mossad/IDF officer turned US security consultant (who appeared in Baron Cohen’s Who Is America? TV series ), and a new figure: Dr Nira Cain-N’Degrocello, a grotesquely supercilious white liberal who is the self-appointed scourge of cultural appropriation. The dupes are built into a big silly climax fabricated with body doubles and (presumably) covert reshooting. Continue reading...

articles.content: The beloved high school TV show is returning in a different political climate. I’m skeptical that Ryan Murphy has the nuance this moment needs For months, Ryan Murphy has been discussing Glee . In July, he expressed his love for the musical comedy drama he created. In September, he said that he had finished writing a pilot for a potential reboot, adding that he had reached out to some of the cast about a reunion. And now it is official : Disney+ and Hulu have commissioned a Glee revival. Glee, which ran for six seasons between 2009 and 2015, was a cultural juggernaut during its initial tenure . The show won six Emmys, four Golden Globes and made stars of actors including Lea Michele, Jonathan Groff, Chris Colfer , Darren Criss and the late Cory Monteith and Naya Rivera. Centred on the trials of New Directions, a scrappy show choir at the fictional McKinley high school in Ohio, the show became known for its peppy covers of show tunes, 80s power pop hits such as Journey’s Don’t Stop Believin’ (a Glee signature), 2010s chart-toppers and some truly baffling mashups (the amalgamation of Scissor Sisters’ Let’s Have a Kiki and Turkey Lurkey Time from Promises, Promises remains … a choice). articles.title: Amy Winehouse: Back to Black 20 review – trying an all-star Amy tribute show is a losing game
articles.summary: (Roundhouse, London) With Jorja Smith, Mark Ronson and others reinterpreting Back to Black for its 20th anniversary, most of the singers are eclipsed by the memory of Winehouse It’s 20 years since Amy Winehouse released her masterpiece Back to Black and 15…
articles.content: (Roundhouse, London) With Jorja Smith, Mark Ronson and others reinterpreting Back to Black for its 20th anniversary, most of the singers are eclipsed by the memory of Winehouse It’s 20 years since Amy Winehouse released her masterpiece Back to Black and 15 since she died at a frighteningly young age. A good way to appreciate how special she was is to watch the Amy Winehouse Band trot through a few lesser songs and cover versions and spot what’s missing: her playfulness, bite, anarchic charisma and taste. Winehouse mixed soul, jazz, hip-hop, two-tone and 60s girl groups because she loved that music more than anything. Without her animating fandom, a cover of Monkey Man by Toots and the Maytals is just a cover of Monkey Man by Toots and the Maytals; for all her old band’s precision and gusto, it has no pressing reason to exist. The main event, in which Back to Black producers including Mark Ronson and Salaam Remi hand-pick singers such as Jorja Smith, Lianne La Havas and Corinne Bailey Rae to recreate the album, is stronger except that it’s primarily staged for a BBC TV show, which means the flow is broken by onstage interviews and hagiographical patter from Jo Whiley. It’s a little grating to be constantly told that a concert is amazing even as it unfolds, but that’s TV for you. Continue reading...

articles.content: The Scrubs and Garden State star answers your questions about working with megastars, getting his hair to look good and being brutally killed on BoJack Horseman How do you manage not to act starstruck when directing people like Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine and Harrison Ford? TopTramp That’s where my acting comes in – I pretend that I don’t know how famous they are. Every actor really wants a leader. They want someone who knows the script really well, has a plan for how the scene is going to be executed, and – in the case of comedy – knows how to make it funny. The last thing any of those guys wants is someone coming in starstruck and wide-eyed. So I use my acting skills to pretend I’m not starstruck and treat them like normal people. Your Fake Doctors, Real Friends podcast was a real help through lockdown. You were very emotionally open and personal; it was like catching up with friends. I still think about your line that making it in acting, even if you’re talented and good-looking, is like winning the lottery. Do you think that early 00s Zach Braff would make it in the present day the way you did? KamesJ Back then, the broadcast networks were making so many pilots, at least it was work for people. Now, I think it’s a much harder landscape to break through. I firmly believe that you can be talented and good-looking, but success is still like winning the lottery. I know plenty of brilliant actors whose lottery ticket hasn’t come up yet. I started auditioning at 14 and barely got anything for years, so I’ve always felt very lucky. Continue reading...
